note: Maintained calendar. Dated entries come from the gazetted public holiday lists (2026: Government Printing Department; 2027: Central Bank of Sri Lanka) or an official announcement. Entries with dateConfirmed=false are recurring seasons shown by month only.

events.title: Duruthu Full Moon Poya Day
events.description: Marks the Buddha's first visit to Sri Lanka. The Duruthu Perahera is held at Kelaniya Raja Maha Vihara. Poya days are public holidays: alcohol and meat sales are closed and many visit temples dressed in white.
events.source: Government Printing Department – 2026 public holiday calendar

events.title: Tamil Thai Pongal Day
events.description: Tamil harvest festival giving thanks to the sun. Families boil the first rice of the harvest with milk and jaggery until it overflows.
events.source: Government Printing Department – 2026 public holiday calendar

events.title: Navam Full Moon Poya Day
events.description: Marks the appointment of the two chief disciples. Gangaramaya temple in Colombo holds the Navam Perahera. Poya days are public holidays: alcohol and meat sales are closed and many visit temples dressed in white.
events.source: Government Printing Department – 2026 public holiday calendar

events.title: National Independence Day
events.description: Commemorates independence on 4 February 1948. The national ceremony and parade are held in Colombo.
events.source: Government Printing Department – 2026 public holiday calendar

events.title: Maha Shivaratri
events.description: The great night of Lord Shiva. Hindu devotees fast and keep an all-night vigil; Koneswaram in Trincomalee and Ketheeswaram in Mannar draw large crowds.
events.source: Government Printing Department – 2026 public holiday calendar

events.title: Medin Full Moon Poya Day
events.description: Marks the Buddha's visit to his father's kingdom of Kapilavastu. Poya days are public holidays: alcohol and meat sales are closed and many visit temples dressed in white.
events.source: Government Printing Department – 2026 public holiday calendar

events.title: Eid ul-Fitr (Ramazan Festival)
events.description: Marks the end of the Ramadan fast with prayers, family visits and festive food.
events.source: Government Printing Department – 2026 public holiday calendar

events.title: Bak Full Moon Poya Day
events.description: Marks the Buddha's second visit to Sri Lanka, at Nagadeepa. Poya days are public holidays: alcohol and meat sales are closed and many visit temples dressed in white.
events.source: Government Printing Department – 2026 public holiday calendar

events.title: Good Friday
events.description: Christians commemorate the crucifixion of Jesus with services and passion plays.
events.source: Government Printing Department – 2026 public holiday calendar

events.title: Day before Sinhala & Tamil New Year
events.description: Preparations for Aluth Avurudu: houses are cleaned and sweets such as kokis and kavum are made.
events.source: Government Printing Department – 2026 public holiday calendar

events.title: Sinhala & Tamil New Year
events.description: Aluth Avurudu / Puthandu: auspicious times for lighting the hearth and eating the first meal, followed by village games and family visits across the island.
events.source: Government Printing Department – 2026 public holiday calendar

events.title: Vesak Full Moon Poya Day
events.description: Commemorates the birth, enlightenment and passing of the Buddha. Streets are decorated with lanterns, thoranas and dansal. Poya days are public holidays: alcohol and meat sales are closed and many visit temples dressed in white.
events.source: Government Printing Department – 2026 public holiday calendar

events.title: International Labour Day
events.description: Public holiday. Political rallies and processions take place in Colombo and other cities.
events.source: Government Printing Department – 2026 public holiday calendar

events.title: State Vesak Week
events.description: The government moved the 2026 State Vesak festival and Vesak week to 27 May – 2 June, centred on the full moon of 30 May. Expect lantern displays, thoranas and dansal across the island.
events.source: Ministry of Public Administration statement (Vesak 2026)

events.title: Eid ul-Adha (Hajj Festival)
events.description: Festival of sacrifice marking the end of the Hajj pilgrimage, with prayers and the sharing of food.
events.source: Government Printing Department – 2026 public holiday calendar

events.title: Adhi Poson Full Moon Poya Day
events.description: The additional (leap) lunar month of Poson. Poya days are public holidays: alcohol and meat sales are closed and many visit temples dressed in white.
events.source: Government Printing Department – 2026 public holiday calendar

events.title: Poson Full Moon Poya Day
events.description: Marks the arrival of Arahat Mahinda and Buddhism in Sri Lanka. Pilgrims gather at Mihintale. Poya days are public holidays: alcohol and meat sales are closed and many visit temples dressed in white.
events.source: Government Printing Department – 2026 public holiday calendar

events.title: Esala Full Moon Poya Day
events.description: Marks the Buddha's first sermon and the start of the Vas rains retreat. Season of the great peraheras. Poya days are public holidays: alcohol and meat sales are closed and many visit temples dressed in white.
events.source: Government Printing Department – 2026 public holiday calendar

events.title: Madhu Church Feast
events.description: Feast of the Assumption at the Shrine of Our Lady of Madhu, the largest Catholic pilgrimage in Sri Lanka. Pilgrims arrive in the days before 15 August.
events.source: Feast of the Assumption (fixed date, 15 August)

events.title: Kandy Esala Perahera
events.description: Ten nights of processions with nearly 100 elephants, drummers and dancers honouring the Sacred Tooth Relic. Kumbal Perahera 18–22 August, Randoli Perahera 23–27 August, closing day procession 28 August.
events.source: Sri Dalada Maligawa (via Newsfirst)

events.title: Milad-un-Nabi
events.description: Celebrates the birth of the Prophet Muhammad.
events.source: Government Printing Department – 2026 public holiday calendar

events.title: Nikini Full Moon Poya Day
events.description: Commemorates the First Buddhist Council. Poya days are public holidays: alcohol and meat sales are closed and many visit temples dressed in white.
events.source: Government Printing Department – 2026 public holiday calendar

events.title: Binara Full Moon Poya Day
events.description: Commemorates the founding of the order of Buddhist nuns (Bhikkhuni Sasana). Poya days are public holidays: alcohol and meat sales are closed and many visit temples dressed in white.
events.source: Government Printing Department – 2026 public holiday calendar

events.title: Vap Full Moon Poya Day
events.description: Marks the end of the Vas rains retreat; Kathina robe-offering ceremonies follow. Poya days are public holidays: alcohol and meat sales are closed and many visit temples dressed in white.
events.source: Government Printing Department – 2026 public holiday calendar

events.title: Deepavali
events.description: The Hindu festival of lights. Homes are lit with oil lamps and decorated with kolam, and sweets are shared.
events.source: Government Printing Department – 2026 public holiday calendar

events.title: Il Full Moon Poya Day
events.description: Marks the Buddha sending out his first sixty disciples to spread the Dhamma. Poya days are public holidays: alcohol and meat sales are closed and many visit temples dressed in white.
events.source: Government Printing Department – 2026 public holiday calendar

events.title: Unduvap Full Moon Poya Day
events.description: Commemorates Sanghamitta Theri bringing the sapling of the Sri Maha Bodhi to Anuradhapura. The Sri Pada pilgrimage season begins. Poya days are public holidays: alcohol and meat sales are closed and many visit temples dressed in white.
events.source: Government Printing Department – 2026 public holiday calendar

events.title: Sri Pada (Adam's Peak) pilgrimage season
events.description: The pilgrimage season runs from Unduvap Poya in December to Vesak Poya in May. Climbers start at night from Nallathanniya to see sunrise from the summit.
events.source: Season runs Unduvap Poya to Vesak Poya (official Poya dates)

events.title: Christmas Day
events.description: Midnight masses, carols and Christmas decorations in towns such as Colombo and Negombo.
events.source: Government Printing Department – 2026 public holiday calendar

events.title: Whale watching season – Mirissa
events.description: Blue whales and dolphins off the south coast. Boats leave Mirissa harbour early morning; the sea is calmest between December and April.
events.source: Recurring season (south-west monsoon off-season)

events.title: Surf season – Arugam Bay
events.description: The east coast surf season, with point breaks at Main Point, Whiskey Point and Peanut Farm.
events.source: Recurring season (east coast dry season)

events.title: Nallur Kandaswamy Festival
events.description: A 25-day temple festival in Jaffna with daily processions, ending with the chariot festival (Ther) and water-cutting (Theertham). Dates are announced by the temple each year.
events.source: Usually August–September; confirm with the temple

events.title: Kataragama Esala Festival
events.description: Buddhists, Hindus and Muslims share this festival at Kataragama, with nightly peraheras; many pilgrims walk the Pada Yatra through Yala and Kumana.
events.source: Usually July–August; dates announced locally

events.title: Navaratri & Saraswathi Pooja
events.description: Nine nights honouring the goddesses Durga, Lakshmi and Saraswathi, ending with Vijayadashami; schools and offices hold Saraswathi Pooja for learning and the arts.
events.source: Hindu lunar calendar (September–October)

events.title: Galle Literary Festival
events.description: Readings, talks and workshops inside the Galle Fort heritage area. Check the festival website for this year’s dates.
events.source: Usually January; confirm on the festival website
